verdict.rationale: Viam's first-party docs cover each bring-up step. A guided wizard creates a machine and installs viam-server, and you search the Registry by hardware model. viam-server then pulls and initializes the driver from the config, and a discovery service suggests component configurations. First motion can be tested from web test panels (drive bases, move arms) or through the motion service. A community reading notes the robot needs a Linux-class OS with a TCP stack, which narrows the scope but does not contradict the claim. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the hours-not-weeks bring-up time; documented bring-up for hardware lacking an existing Registry driver or a Linux-capable host.
